messages:
SRE-Bot: incident-bot fired: ALERT: backend.latency.p99.europe > 6000ms (threshold 2000ms) — PagerDuty page created (PD-INC-8421)
PagerDuty: PagerDuty: Triggered: PD-INC-8421 — policy=latency-p99-eu, urgency=high, service=runtime-gateway
maria (oncall): acked PD-INC-8421 — I'm on it, looking into EU west frontends/sidecars first :eyes:
jonathan (runtime): seeing p99 spikes on sidecar proxies. KV cache miss rates spiking ~5x. Logs show `sidecar/evict` messages around the same time.
leo (infra): autoscaler reports rapid scale-in then backfill, CPU on redis nodes at 90%. Could be cache thrash from a bad workqueue.
manual ops-bot: last deploy for `gateway-sidecar` was 2026-03-14T09:12:04Z by ci-bot. No rollbacks since.
maria (oncall): copying relevant graphs: `grafana/dashboard?panel=latency_p99&region=eu-west` — p99 jumped from ~1800ms to 7k around 09:16 UTC
jonathan (runtime): running quick tail on sidecar logs:```json
{"ts":"2026-03-14T09:15:52Z","msg":"evicting-prefix","prefix":"/kv/ctx/","reason":"memory_pressure"}
{"ts":"2026-03-14T09:15:53Z","msg":"evicting-prefix","prefix":"/kv/ctx/","reason":"memory_pressure"}
```
jonathan (runtime): that sequence looks like hot prefix thrash; requests bouncing to origin causing long tails. Could correlate with a traffic spike or a bad client pattern.
anika (oncall-next): tagging load test? Any deploy that might have introduced more aggressive prefetching?
leo (infra): checking LB logs: small burst from a handful of IPs hitting long-prefixed keys, consistent with a downstream job. No new release in past 6h for client code.
maria (oncall): immediate mitigations: 1) scale redis cluster + add read replicas 2) enable fallback routing to `model-compact` for non-critical routes 3) temporarily raise sidecar cache size/shrink eviction aggressiveness
maria (oncall): running scale command now:```bash
kubectl -n prod scale statefulset redis-eu --replicas=5
kubectl -n prod patch cm sidecar-config -p '{"data":{"cache.eviction_threshold":"0.85"}}'
```
ops-bot: command accepted, scaling in progress — redis-eu replicas scaling to 5 (estimated 90s)
leo (infra): starting vertical pod autoscaler override for sidecar to bump mem requests for current pods, will roll one at a time.
jonathan (runtime): also enabling model fallback route: `traffic.router.set_region_policy(eu-west, fallback_model='model-compact-v2')` — doing a 5% canary -> 100% if green
maria (oncall): toggled canary to 5% now. watching latency and error rates.
SRE-Bot: PD-INC-8421 acknowledged by maria (oncall). Notification: automated escalate in 12m if not resolved.
customer-support: FYI we have two customer reports about timeouts in EU: CS-3214, CS-3215. I pinged both with short note.
jonathan (runtime): after initial scale & small config bump, p99 down to ~3k at 09:19, errors still a little elevated. KV miss rate dropping.
maria (oncall): rolling a mitigation: temporarily mute an identified noisy client IP range at the LB layer:```bash
curl -X POST \ "https://lb-api.internal/v1/blocks" -d '{"cidr":"203.0.113.0/24","reason":"noisy-client-causing-kv-thrash"}'
```
leo (infra): block in place. dropped ~12% of traffic that matched noisy pattern — p99 improved to ~1.6k by 09:22 UTC
anika (oncall-next): nice. is there customer impact after block?
maria (oncall): CS reports look like timeouts for a small subset of customers tied to that IP range; I asked CS to escalate impacted accounts. overall platform SLO still breached but trending back under.
PagerDuty: PD-INC-8421 status: acknowledged, responders: maria (oncall)
jonathan (runtime): recommending post-incident actions: 1) add sentinel alert for rapid prefix eviction surges 2) harden sidecar eviction thresholds per workload 3) throttle clients at LB where possible 4) create synthetic check to detect noisy patterns earlier
maria (oncall): agreed. creating incident doc: `/incidents/2026-03-14-eu-sidecar-thrash.md` with timeline + customer list.
maria (oncall): handoff note incoming — I need to grab lunch in ~20m, will hand off active watch to anika (oncall-next). leaving a checklist in incident doc.
anika (oncall-next): standing by, will monitor dashboards and escalate to runtime if regression. if p99 creeps back above 3k we call PD escalation.
SRE-Bot: PD-INC-8421 will auto-escalate at 09:34 UTC if status not resolved (remaining 11m).
maria (oncall): summary for handoff: mitigation steps taken: scaled redis + patch sidecar config, LB block for noisy CIDR, enabled fallback routing for non-critical routes, canary -> observing. Primary impact: increased p99 latency in eu-west between 09:15-09:24, affecting some customer requests and causing 2 support tickets.
customer-support: noted. will follow up with affected customers and gather logs for RCA requests.
leo (infra): I'll follow up on autoscaler behavior and add a guard to prevent aggressive scale-in during traffic oscillations.
jonathan (runtime): I'll draft the postmortem and config changes. will include the `evict` sentinel and guidance for workload-specific cache sizing.
maria (oncall): handing off to anika now — I'm switching status to `briefing` and adding notes in doc. back to oncall rotation later tonight. thanks all :thumbsup:
anika (oncall-next): ack — taking watch. ping me if anything spikes.
SRE-Bot: PD-INC-8421 marked as monitored. Incident still open until SLO restored and customer tickets triaged.
PagerDuty: PD-INC-8421 remains open — no further escalation triggered.
---
(incident follow-up summary will be appended to `/incidents/2026-03-14-eu-sidecar-thrash.md`)
